issues.passage: Critics called the brand-new design reminiscent of nothing anyone could associate with prior work.
issues.why: Valid English: 'reminiscent of nothing…' means the design evokes no prior associations (i.e., it is unprecedented). That is correct use of reminiscent = tending to remind one of something, with a negative complement.

fix.correctPassage: The café's tiled floor was reminiscent of the station waiting room she had known as a child.
wrongPassages: Critics called the brand-new design reminiscent even though it reminded them of nothing at all.
He stayed carefully reminiscent so that no detail of the past would ever come to mind.
A completely blank memory made the faded photograph feel intensely reminiscent of her childhood.
